title: Redis: scale-up a replica VM (CPU + RAM, round-trip)
description: Vertically resizes a Redis VM with the FULLY-IMPLEMENTED scale-up verb (GAP #13, batch 3). The VmrunVmResizer powers off via vmrun, makes an atomic .vmx edit (numvcpus / memsize), cold-starts, and reports old->new. It is cluster-aware: it resolves redis's owning adapter, warms its status, and consults RedisAdapter.CanResizeVm -- refusing the current write-primary unless --force-primary. NOTE: vms.yaml labels redis-1 the shard1 primary BY DESIGN, but Redis Cluster master/replica roles drift at runtime; the gate reads the LIVE role. Step 1 confirms the live role before resizing (resize a node only while it is a replica, or pass --force-primary). Live-verified 2026-07-05 on redis-1: cpu 2->4->2, ram 2048->3072->2048 (guest nproc=4, MemTotal ~3 GB), then a clean scale-DOWN back.

prerequisites.smokeGate: nexus-infra-oltp smoke-0.G.1 ALL GREEN; build host = Windows (vmrun + vmware-vdiskmanager on PATH via VmrunPaths)

observe.what: the live role of each node; confirm the resize target (redis-1) is currently a REPLICA -> the cluster-safety gate will allow the resize. If it is a live master, fail it over first or pass --force-primary.
JSON: outcome=ok; oldCpu 2 -> newCpu 4; oldRamMb 2048 -> newRamMb 3072; durationSec ~30-60 (graceful guest shutdown + atomic .vmx edit + cold start)
guest now reports 4 CPUs and MemTotal ~3072 MB -- the .vmx edit took effect on cold boot
redis-1 settings show 4 processors + 3 GB RAM
scale-DOWN back to 2 CPU / 2048 MB (right-sized per feedback_prefer_less_memory) -- resize is bidirectional and idempotent; re-running with the same values returns outcome=skipped

whatProves: scale-up is a real, bidirectional vertical resizer (cpu + ram via atomic .vmx edit + cold restart) and is cluster-aware: it resizes a Redis replica with no impact to the shard's surviving primary, and would refuse the live write-primary without --force-primary.
